normalized_issues.title: Vocabulary decoration write requires entry_id before the turn entry exists

merged_from.title: Vocabulary decoration write requires an entry_id before the turn entry exists

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-00 Seam G requires vocabulary resolution BEFORE tool-call construction, and SPEC-07 Stage 5 requires durable decoration persistence as part of that resolution. But the DHF entry (which provides the entry_id the decoration references) is only created at turn completion via AppendTurnAsync. No mechanism is defined for obtaining or reserving an entry_id at vocabulary-resolution time, making the decoration write contract impossible to implement as specified.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00: 'The agent loop calls IVocabularyResolver ... BEFORE constructing tool calls.' and 'Upon turn completion ... hands it to DhfLedger.AppendTurnAsync.' SPEC-07 §3.1 Stage 5: 'Awaits SPEC-04 DhfDecorationWriter INSERT' and §8.2: 'The decoration is linked to the agent-turn entry (via entry_id)'.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Choose one explicit mechanism: (a) SPEC-07 returns the decoration payload only; SPEC-05 persists it after AppendTurnAsync returns an entry_id, or (b) define a preallocated turn identifier created before vocabulary resolution and carried through the lifecycle. Update SPEC-00 Seam G, SPEC-07 §3.1/§8.2, and SPEC-05 to reflect the chosen path.

normalized_issues.title: SPEC-04 defines contradictory hash input sets in adjacent sections

merged_from.title: SPEC-04 defines contradictory entry hash inputs
SPEC-04 defines incompatible hash inputs in adjacent sections

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-04 §4.2 DhfHashColumns includes 'entry_id', 'session_id', 'sequence_number' in the hashed column list. SPEC-04 §4.2a explicitly lists those same three columns as 'NOT included in DhfHashColumns'. The hash contract has two conflicting definitions, meaning append and validation will compute different record_hash values from the same row.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-04 §4.2 HashedColumns array includes 'entry_id', 'session_id', 'sequence_number'. SPEC-04 §4.2a table lists entry_id as 'Identity, not content', session_id as 'Identity link to parent row', and sequence_number as 'Ordering only' — all excluded.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Make one hashed-column list authoritative and remove the contradictory statement. Add a build-breaking HashColumnSyncTests assertion that the §4.2a exclusion table and the actual DhfHashColumns set are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive over all dhf.entries columns.

normalized_issues.title: Session closure reason has no schema field or repository API despite being required by SPEC-00

merged_from.title: Session closure reason is required by SPEC-00 but has no schema field or repository API

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-00 Seam C and §6 Glossary define three closure reasons (explicit_shutdown, superseded_session, heartbeat_timeout) and state 'SPEC-04 records a session-closure event noting the reason.' However, dhf.sessions has no closure_reason column, and CloseSessionAsync only executes UPDATE dhf.sessions SET ended_at = NOW() with no reason parameter. The closure reason is unimplementable as specified.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 §6 Glossary DHF Session entry defines three closure reasons. SPEC-04 §6.2 CloseSessionAsync signature: Task CloseSessionAsync(Guid sessionId, CancellationToken ct) — no reason parameter. dhf.sessions schema in migrations 001-009 has no closure_reason column.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a closure_reason TEXT column to dhf.sessions (new migration 010), add a reason parameter to CloseSessionAsync, update all call sites in SPEC-03/SPEC-04, expose it in SessionSummary/SessionDetail DTOs, and add it to the guard_session_update trigger's permitted-transition list. Alternatively, explicitly downgrade closure reason to log-only in every spec and remove the SPEC-00 claim.

normalized_issues.title: ACC identifiers 25-27 are assigned to different capabilities in SPEC-00 and SPEC-07

merged_from.title: ACC identifiers 25-27 are assigned to different capabilities in SPEC-00 and SPEC-07
Acceptance-test IDs ACC-25/26/27 are assigned to different meanings in SPEC-00 and SPEC-07

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-00 §3 assigns ACC-25 to durable session lock, ACC-26 to recovery-event persistence, ACC-27 to neutral landing page. SPEC-07 §12 assigns ACC-25 to multi-domain resolution, ACC-26 to decoration-write durability/circuit-breaker, ACC-27 to bouncer-cache raw-utterance isolation. The global acceptance-test namespace is no longer unique.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 §3 ACC table rows for ACC-25/26/27. SPEC-07 §12 ACC table rows for ACC-25/26/27. Both sets are present in the same document bundle.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Renumber SPEC-07 additions to ACC-28, ACC-29, ACC-30 (or next available). Update the SPEC-00 master ACC table to include the SPEC-07 entries under the new numbers. Update all cross-references in SPEC-07 §11 test names and SPEC-00 §3 never-descopable gate list.

normalized_issues.title: Viewer entry-detail endpoint lacks session-capability access control

merged_from.title: Entry-detail API breaks the session-capability access model

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-06 §5.1 and §5.2 define GET /api/dhf/entries/{entryId} with no sessionId requirement. The spec acknowledges 'the entry ID alone does not grant access' but relies on sidebar link hiding rather than server-side authorization. Anyone who obtains an entryId can fetch full entry content including screenshots and tool-call details, bypassing the URL-as-capability boundary.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-06 §5.1: 'the entry ID alone does not grant access; the session sidebar hides entries from other sessions.' No sessionId validation is specified in the endpoint contract. SPEC-06 SDR-06-007 defines the capability model as sessionId-based.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Require a valid sessionId capability on every entry-detail request. Verify the requested entryId belongs to the session identified by the capability before returning data. Add SessionCapabilityGateTests coverage for the entry-detail endpoint.

normalized_issues.title: Locked same-AddinSessionId sessions on other workstations are silently bypassed during session open

merged_from.title: Locked same-AddinSessionId sessions on other workstations are ignored during session open

normalized_issues.core_problem: In SPEC-04 §6.1 OpenOrResumeSessionCore, the first lookup filters ended_at IS NULL AND locked_at IS NULL. The second locked-session check adds AND workstation_id = @WorkstationId. A locked open session with the same tenant+AddinSessionId on a different workstation matches neither branch, allowing a new session to be inserted with the same AddinSessionId — bypassing SDR-04-008's cross-workstation hard-error rule.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-04 §6.1 first query: WHERE tenant_id = @TenantId AND addin_session_id = @AddinSessionId AND ended_at IS NULL AND locked_at IS NULL. Second query: WHERE ... AND locked_at IS NOT NULL AND workstation_id = @WorkstationId. No query covers: same AddinSessionId, different workstation, locked.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Before inserting, add a query for any open row (ended_at IS NULL) with the same tenant+AddinSessionId regardless of lock state. If workstation differs, throw CrossWorkstationSessionConflictException. If workstation matches and locked, throw SessionLockedException. Update SessionLockDurabilityTests and CrossWorkstationConflictTests to cover this case.

normalized_issues.title: SPEC-01 contradicts itself on whether ProtocolVersion mismatch can be detected during HTTP upgrade

merged_from.title: SPEC-01 contradicts itself on whether ProtocolVersion mismatch can be detected during HTTP upgrade

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-01 §10 states version mismatch is detected after AddinReadyMessage (post-upgrade). SPEC-01 §9.1 editorial m4 states it is 'caught by §10's version-mismatch handling (HTTP 400 during HTTP upgrade or close code 1002)'. ProtocolVersion is carried in AddinReadyMessage which is sent after upgrade, so HTTP 400 on upgrade is impossible for this failure mode.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-01 §10: 'Add-in sends AddinReadyMessage with ProtocolVersion = Current ... Mismatch → orchestrator sends a version-mismatch error ... then closes the WebSocket.' SPEC-01 §9.1 m4: 'caught by §10's version-mismatch handling (HTTP 400 during HTTP upgrade or close code 1002 during WebSocket protocol-error handling)'.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Remove the HTTP-upgrade variant from §9.1 m4. Define one post-upgrade version-mismatch path: orchestrator sends ClientProtocolErrorMessage(VersionMismatch) then closes with code 1002. Update SameEpochReconnectRejectionTests to cover only the post-upgrade path.

normalized_issues.title: Locked-session recovery runbook is inconsistent across specs

merged_from.title: Locked-session recovery runbook is inconsistent across specs

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-00 Seam C and §6 Glossary say 'operator unlocks the session via SQL' and 'manual SQL unlock is required to resume.' SPEC-04 migration 008 trigger explicitly rejects locked_at non-NULL→NULL transitions and recommends close-and-new-session as the recovery path, treating trigger bypass as last resort. These are contradictory operational procedures.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 §6 Glossary Session Lock: 'manual SQL unlock is required to resume.' SPEC-04 migration 008 comments: 'locked_at may only transition NULL -> non-NULL on session % (unlock requires out-of-band SQL)' and the trigger rejects non-NULL→NULL. SPEC-04 §6.4 unlock section: 'Reversing the lock (non-NULL→NULL) is rejected.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Pick one supported recovery model. Given the trigger design, the correct model is close-and-new-session: update SPEC-00 §6 Glossary and Seam C to say 'operator closes the locked session via SQL and the add-in reconnects with a new AddinSessionId.' Remove all 'unlock and resume' language from SPEC-00.

normalized_issues.title: Viewer mandatory entries endpoint response includes fields absent from IReadOnlyDhfRepository EntryListItem

merged_from.title: Mandatory viewer entries endpoint requests fields absent from the only read-only DTO it is allowed to use

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-06 §4.3 GET /api/dhf/entries response example includes undoOutcome, recordHash, and previousHash. SPEC-04 §9.2 EntryListItem is defined as (EntryId, SequenceNumber, Timestamp, InputModality, TurnType, RawTranscript, ToolCallCount, HasDecorations) — none of the three fields are present. The mandatory endpoint cannot be implemented from the read-only repository without undeclared changes.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-06 §4.3 JSON example: 'undoOutcome', 'recordHash', 'previousHash' fields. SPEC-04 §9.2 EntryListItem record definition: no undoOutcome, recordHash, or previousHash fields.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either extend SPEC-04 §9.2 EntryListItem to include undoOutcome, recordHash, and previousHash, or remove those fields from the SPEC-06 §4.3 response contract. Update DhfRepositoryTests and EntriesEndpointTests accordingly.

normalized_issues.title: Planned disconnect escalation terminates SolidWorks process and loses unrelated unsaved work

merged_from.title: Planned disconnect escalation can terminate SolidWorks and lose unrelated unsaved work

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 §9.1.1 step 7 specifies Environment.Exit(1) after a 5-second grace period when a COM call is stuck. Editorial M4 explicitly acknowledges this 'terminates the SolidWorks process' and that 'unsaved work in other open documents may be lost.' This turns an add-in fault into host-wide data loss for the user.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-02 §9.1.1 step 7: 'the host invokes Environment.Exit(1).' Editorial M4: 'Environment.Exit(1) terminates the SolidWorks process because the add-in runs in-process with SolidWorks. Users see SolidWorks quit without the usual save-prompt; unsaved work in other documents may be lost. Acknowledged degradation, not defect.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Remove Environment.Exit(1) from the in-process add-in path. Instead: mark the add-in session as permanently failed, surface a hard error to the user requiring manual SolidWorks shutdown, and log the stuck call. If forced termination is truly required, move it to an external watchdog process that is not the CAD host. Update PlannedDisconnectEscalationTests to assert no process exit occurs.

normalized_issues.title: Viewer URL-as-capability model enables tenant-wide session enumeration from a single leaked session UUID

merged_from.title: Viewer URL-as-capability model enables tenant-wide session enumeration once any single session UUID is known

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-06 §4.2 and SDR-06-007 explicitly allow GET /api/dhf/sessions?sessionId={uuid} to return all sessions for the tenant that owns the presented session. A single leaked or shoulder-surfed session URL grants an adversary the complete list of all other sessions for that tenant. The spec acknowledges this as an 'accepted v1 trade-off' but does not rate-limit or scope the sidebar endpoint.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 SDR-TL-012: 'Once a caller presents a valid session UUID, they can see other session UUIDs and metadata for the same tenant via the sidebar list... reduces the effective entropy of URL-as-capability from 122 bits per session to 122 bits for first session access within a tenant. Accepted in v1.' SPEC-06 §4.2: returns all tenant sessions given one sessionId.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: For the hackathon/pilot scope, add explicit documentation that the sidebar endpoint must not be used for sessions containing sensitive design IP. For any Medtronic-facing deployment, either remove the tenant-scoped sidebar list (require per-session capability for every fetch) or accelerate Clerk SSO to v1 rather than v1.5. Add a rate limit on the sessions endpoint to slow enumeration.

normalized_issues.title: v2 screenshot viewing path is not representable in the current SPEC-04 read model

merged_from.title: v2 screenshot viewing path is not representable in the current read model

normalized_issues.core_problem: The migration doc §3 v2 contract states 'DHF stores S3 key; viewer and Anthropic vision API fetch via the presigned GET URL.' SPEC-04 §9.2 EntryDetail read-side DTO exposes only byte[]? ScreenshotBeforePng / ScreenshotAfterPng. SPEC-06 §5.2 claims screenshotBefore.dataUrl can be 'https://... presigned (v2)' but there is no S3 key or URL field in the read model to source this from.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Migration doc §3 v2: 'DHF stores S3 key.' SPEC-04 §9.2 EntryDetail: only ScreenshotBeforePng/ScreenshotAfterPng byte arrays. SPEC-06 §5.2 field table: 'screenshotBefore.dataUrl: data:image/png;base64,... (v1) or https://... presigned (v2)' — no corresponding field in SPEC-04 read DTO.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Introduce a version-agnostic screenshot reference DTO now (e.g., a discriminated union with bytes-or-url variants plus sha256 and optional S3 key) in SPEC-04 §9.2 EntryDetail and mirror it in SPEC-06 §5.2. This avoids a breaking cross-spec DTO change during v1→v2 migration.

normalized_issues.title: BSMS hallucination-resistance claim depends on mocked LLM tests with no live semantic enforcement

merged_from.title: BSMS 'structurally hallucination-resistant' claim depends on untested LLM bouncer/synthesizer outputs with no build-time semantic enforcement

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-07 §11 explicitly states 'Live LLM calls are NOT build-breaking... Uses recorded/mocked Sonnet responses.' The entire BSMS safety argument rests on the bouncer and synthesizer producing correct structured JSON, but only the parser is tested in CI. Model updates, temperature variance, or prompt drift can produce malformed output that triggers circuit-breaker session lock without any build-time detection.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-07 §11: 'Live LLM calls are NOT build-breaking (v1.1.0 fix R1-008). CI uses recorded/mocked Sonnet responses; live-model latency and semantic checks run in a separate scheduled canary that does not gate merges.' SPEC-07 §3.3 failure table: MalformedBouncerOutput → VocabularyResolutionFailure; circuit breaker → LockSessionAsync.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a build-breaking prompt-checksum test (BouncerPromptSyncTests already exists — extend it to also verify the recorded mock responses were generated from the current prompt version). Add at least one build-breaking canary that calls the live model with a fixed seed utterance and asserts the rejection_code closed-enum invariant. Document the prompt version in a vocab.bouncer_prompts table.

normalized_issues.title: SPEC-00 claims 'interfaces only, no implementation' but embeds SQL, C# records, test names, and migration scripts

merged_from.title: SPEC-00 claims 'interfaces only, no implementation' but is filled with SQL, C# records, exact test names, migration scripts, and implementation rationales

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-00 §0 states 'Non-goals for this document: state machine details, record field definitions, SQL schemas, build sequence.' Yet SPEC-00 contains full SQL for migrations 007-009, C# record definitions for RecoveryEventContext, test names (HeartbeatTimeoutTcpAbortTests), and implementation trade-off rationales. This creates tight coupling and makes independent per-module Oracle reviews harder.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SPEC-00 §0 Non-goals list. SPEC-00 SDR-TL-013 Consequences section: full SQL migration 009, C# DhfTurnContext field additions, test names. SPEC-00 SDR-TL-014: full C# record definition for AddinTeardownMessage.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: This is a documentation hygiene issue rather than an implementation blocker. The implementation details in SPEC-00 are duplicated from the per-module specs and kept in sync. For future revisions, move implementation details to owning specs and keep SPEC-00 to seam contracts and cross-cutting SDRs. Low priority given the hackathon timeline.

dropped_findings.title: Recovery event persistence model chose 'hackathon-scope' complexity reduction while surrounding text claims regulatory foundation for 21 CFR Part 11
dropped_findings.reason: too_vague — the spec already contains an explicit disclaimer (SDR-TL-006 v1.5.0 clarification) that 'foundation' means architectural readiness, not compliance. The same-table vs separate-table design choice is a legitimate engineering trade-off documented with rationale. The finding conflates the regulatory framing disclaimer (which is accurate) with the implementation choice (which is defensible). No actionable contradiction exists beyond what is already acknowledged.
